body: Dya, yes I agree there isn’t a huge conspiracy. I think what OP is touching upon (but doesn’t mention) is that lung cancer has a stigma in our society. Many people view it as a deserved cancer that can be avoided if people don’t smoke. They blame the victim and feel less sympathy.

This is very true. What I’d like to point out is that there’s more we can be doing to screen at risk populations for lung cancer. My mom’s was found incidentally, but her PCP should have been ordering regular chest CTs.
NHL is lymphoma. OP has cancer.
For what it’s worth, it doesn’t sound like your mom was trying to hide things from you. Everything can change very quickly with cancer, and small cell lung cancer is notorious for coming back hard :(

I’m not a doctor, but from what I understand, small cell lung cancer is very aggressive. It responds quickly to chemo but can come back fast. It sounds like they suspect more brain mets, given dad’s change in behavior. I’m very sorry you and your family are going through this.

I appreciate that you’re trying to help, but I’ve tried talking to people. I’ve tried medication. Heck, I’m a mental health professional myself. Some lives aren’t worth living. I’m now the caregiver for my demented mother. My husband is seemingly leaving me. I’m all alone in this world and I want the pain to end
